observationsNotFindings: STRUCTURAL THINNESS, EXAMINED AND NOT CHARGED. At 4549 bytes this file is roughly an eighth the size of the harness specifications I accepted this session (G19 33369, G22 39418, G23 38890), and eighteen top-level keys present in ALL THREE of those accepted siblings are absent here: whatThisCloses, failsIf, liveCellMemberSplit, namedCorpusClasses, namedCorpusNotAuthored, namedCorpusNote, namedExecutesLimbNote, passProperty, platforms, proposedLaterWork, discipline, sliceStanding, namingStandingCarried, windowsStanding, liveAssuranceStageVerbatim, liveStatusVerbatim, condition2StandingCarried and condition5StandingCarried. Both members also omit the measures field that all three siblings carry. I looked hard for a defect behind the thinness and did not find one: every cell the file does carry is character-exact, both members carry exactByteIntent and passProperty, every governance claim verifies, and every attack in this cycle's dispatch is refuted. Thinness that leaves the live obligations correctly stated is not a defect I will manufacture. But the coordinator should see the gap plainly, because a fuller v2 in the family's form would carry an explicit OBL id, a failsIf list, a corpus block, and a quantified pass domain, and would cost little.

decision.summaryForCoordinator: No blockers, no SHOULD-FIX, but this one deserves a caveat rather than a clean bill. Everything the file asserts verifies: 2/2 cited digests, all five carried cells character-exact against the live row located by line prefix, the two-member semicolon split derived and rejoined exactly, both members carrying exactByteIntent and passProperty, D-152 and D-077 accurate clause by clause, and both G17 standing tokens confirmed live - INAPPLICABLE-DROPPED-BY-D077 is the actual sliceStanding on naming v6's DR-G17 entry, not a minted token, and SARIF_for_analyze appears in its rides field. The right NT-5 is pinned: DR-131 NT-5 is sarif-not-advertised, distinct from DR-133 NT-5 coverage-domain-mutation which I verified at G23, and the file pins the namespace twice. Every attack in the dispatch is refuted. What I want on the record is that at 4549 bytes this file is about an eighth the size of the three harness specifications I accepted this session, and eighteen top-level keys common to all three are absent - among them whatThisCloses, failsIf, a corpus block, a platforms block and a top-level passProperty - along with the measures field on both members. I probed the three places that thinness could hide a defect: the purpose sentence promising corpus intent the file states only distributively inside EV-1; the bare 'NT-5' where the live tail reads 'refuse-or-not-offer corpus (DR-131 NT-5)'; and the live 'pass all' carried verbatim but bound to no enumerated domain. None of the three is false against live bytes and none admits a wrong pass, so I charge none of them. A v2 in the family's form would close all three cheaply. 20 attacks run, 20 refuted.
